papers.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience

summary.tldr: Player-1 is a post-training framework that uses synthetic experience and PPO reinforcement learning to significantly improve computer-use agent performance across complex 2D and 3D games.
key_points: Extended standard computer-use action spaces to include relative pointer motion, sustained inputs, and composite actions combining multiple keyboard/mouse inputs.
Fine-tuned models on 6,044 curated gameplay trajectories featuring visual reasoning, task instructions, and paired actions for supervised initialization.
Constructed Player-1-Gym, consisting of 16 synthetic 2D/3D environments with randomized observations, control dynamics, and programmatically verifiable rewards for multi-environment PPO training.

Player-1-9B achieved a 38.33% success rate on MineDojo-300 (up 27.8 percentage points over its SFT baseline), outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline of 12.63%, with additional gains on ViZDoom-10 and GameWorld.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that training agents in synthetic, procedurally randomized environments with composite action spaces enables broad zero-shot transfer to complex, unseen interactive visual environments.

papers.title: RuleTrek: Benchmarking Agentic Rule Reasoning in Complex Scenarios

summary.tldr: RuleTrek is a new multi-domain benchmark that evaluates agentic rule reasoning across complex, multi-file scenarios in interactive workspaces.
key_points: Constructed via a pipeline that extracts structured rule graphs, then generates and composes consistent, solvable rule-specific sub-scenarios.
Evaluates three specific capabilities in interactive workspaces: Rule Identification (RI), Rule Deduction (RD), and End-to-End Rule Reasoning (E2E).
Benchmark results across 11 frontier LLMs demonstrate low performance, with peak scores reaching only 62.47% for RI, 60.43% for RD, and between 26.97% and 55.29% for E2E.
summary.why_it_matters: It reveals that state-of-the-art LLM agents struggle to identify and deductively apply domain-specific rules when factual information is distributed across complex file environments.

papers.title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory

summary.tldr: Cortex internalizes context-induced performance gains into LLM parametric memory using query generation and mergeable low-rank or structural FFN updates without losing non-target capabilities.
key_points: Formulates Memory Consolidation (MC) to unify context-specified editing, skill learning, and behavioral steering into a shared objective.

Introduces Cortex, a method that generates prospective queries to anticipate context use and distills context-conditioned outputs into mergeable low-rank or structural feed-forward network (FFN) updates.
Evaluates performance across 4B to 120B dense and mixture-of-experts backbones, covering both text-only and multimodal architectures.
Achieves 88.9% recovery of context-induced gains while retaining 99.8% of original non-target performance after 50 sequential factual edits on a 14B parameter model using Cortex-Structural.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables large language models to permanently retain new skills and factual edits from context without requiring perpetual context window usage or degrading base model capabilities.

papers.title: ActionOPD: Distilling Decisions, Not Tokens

summary.tldr: ActionOPD is an action-level, on-policy distillation method that aligns student model decisions with black-box teacher decisions using semantic action agreement rewards instead of token-level probabilities.
key_points: Eliminates the requirement for identical tokenizers or access to teacher token probabilities by operating at the semantic action level.
Addresses state-distribution mismatch by using on-policy distillation, sampling actions from both student and teacher at student-encountered states.
Improves Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B performance by 3.3 to 6.9 percentage points on average across four out-of-distribution tool-use benchmarks.
Supports Self-ActionOPD configurations using a same-model teacher supplied with privileged context.
Achieves competitive performance on the τ^2-bench compared to standard offline distillation and token-level OPD.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables effective distillation of proprietary, black-box, or cross-tokenizer teacher models into smaller student agents without forcing the student to imitate teacher reasoning tokens.

papers.title: Apertus 1.5: From Open Text Models to Open Multimodal Reasoners

summary.tldr: Apertus 1.5 extends open text models to multimodal reasoning via continued pretraining, expanding context windows to 262k tokens and adding image and audio understanding without changing the base LM architecture.
key_points: Continued pretraining uses 4T additional tokens for the 8B model and 2T for the 70B model, adding multimodality strictly through the tokenizer.
Extends the context window fourfold to 262,144 tokens while maintaining a text-only language-model head output.
Introduces reasoning via a chat template flag rather than a standalone model, boosting 8B mathematical reasoning performance by up to 20 points.
Post-training pipeline includes supervised finetuning, long-context finetuning, RL with verifiable rewards, and preference alignment based on a published charter.
Trained exclusively on openly available data, respecting crawler opt-outs and excluding restrictively licensed content, with all weights, data recipes, and eval suites permissively released.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that competitive multimodal reasoning models with 262k context windows can be built and fully open-sourced using strictly permissive data and transparent training recipes.

papers.title: KV4-RL: Unlocking Faster Asynchronous Rollouts for RLVR with INT4 KV Cache Quantization

summary.tldr: KV4-RL accelerates RLVR asynchronous rollouts using INT4 KV cache quantization paired with selective INT8 protection for attention sinks and recent context.
key_points: Identifies that sustained concurrency in asynchronous rollouts concentrates context processing into decode steps, making KV cache quantization more effective than weight-only or weight-activation quantization.
Combines calibration-free INT4 KV quantization with selective INT8 protection of a bounded number of attention sinks and recent context tokens to mitigate sampler mismatch and training degradation.

Achieves a 1.80x cumulative rollout speedup and a 1.27x cumulative full-iteration speedup over BF16 across 400 iterations of Qwen3-8B-Base GRPO training, reaching up to 1.97x rollout speedup near the end of training.
Maintains task performance, achieving a final six-benchmark mean accuracy within 0.5 percentage points of full BF16-rollout training for both Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base models.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces memory bandwidth bottlenecks and generation latency in RLVR training without degrading downstream model accuracy.

papers.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents

summary.tldr: HybridAgents dynamically switch between text interaction and latent space reasoning within a single unified generation process, supported by a lightweight HybridLink component and specialized SFT and RL post-training algorithms.
key_points: Architecturally introduces HybridLink for text-latent transitions and continuous working memory to preserve context across multiple turns while maintaining inspectable latent thoughts.

Employs a two-stage post-training pipeline: HybridSFT to stabilize tool-integrated hybrid generation with HybridLink, followed by HybridRL to optimize when to use latent reasoning versus text actions.
Evaluated across 3 model scales and 11 benchmarks covering mathematics, science, medicine, search, and agentic reasoning.
Achieves a 10.4% performance increase over baseline text and latent methods while reducing tokens by 35.5%-54.7%, increasing inference speed by 1.8x-2.6x, and reducing costs by 2.7x-3.7x.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables LLM agents to execute fast, cost-effective internal latent reasoning without sacrificing text-based tool integration or interpretability.

papers.title: τ-Emotion-Bench: Exposing the Interaction Fragility of LLM Agents through Real-World User Emotions

summary.tldr: τ-Emotion-Bench evaluates tool-calling LLM agents across ten domains using emotion-conditioned user interactions, while the Tracer pipeline generates interaction-aware training trajectories.
key_points: Introduces τ-Emotion-Bench, a ten-domain benchmark designed to test long-horizon tool-calling agents against emotional user variations without altering task objectives.
Develops Tracer, an agentic data-generation pipeline that uses an interactive agent-user-environment harness where dissatisfied users can terminate inefficient interactions.
Shows that frontier LLM agents exhibit high interaction fragility, demonstrating large gaps between average task success and consistent task completion.
Proves that Tracer-generated supervision improves Qwen3 models across scales and generalizes to unseen domains, τ-Bench, and τ-Trait.
Identifies that higher agent task success correlates with an optimal balance between tool execution and necessary user follow-ups.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a framework to measure and improve agent reliability in real-world deployments where human users exhibit uncooperative or emotional behavior.

papers.title: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm

summary.tldr: SwarmRSI is a framework that enables scientific agent swarms to achieve recursive self-improvement by mutating and recombining research hypotheses and program components based on experimental feedback.
key_points: Feedback-Guided Swarm Mutation refines research hypotheses and their code implementations using cross-agent experimental feedback.
Complementary Swarm Recombination reuses retained hypotheses and partial program components across agents to support new experiments.
Recursive Swarm Evolution integrates mutation and recombination into an iterative loop where new evidence continuously guides subsequent research.
Achieved SOTA performance on OpenProblems, NatureBench, and MLE-Bench Lite benchmarks.
Demonstrated generalization on held-out tasks and generated programs that were physically reproduced by biologists for follow-up analyses.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables multi-agent systems to leverage partial results and cross-agent feedback to autonomously evolve actionable scientific hypotheses and reproducible software implementations.

papers.title: SkillMarker: A KGW-Based Watermarking Method for Agent Skill Ownership Verification

summary.tldr: SkillMarker adapts the KGW watermarking algorithm to agent skills by combining quality-constrained rewriting with signal-oriented candidate search to protect intellectual property.
key_points: Unifies quality-constrained rewriting to isolate core domain knowledge from flexible phrasing, preserving factual and procedural instruction accuracy.
Uses a signal-oriented candidate search to select high-signal alternative expressions within established quality constraints.
Enables both ownership verification and leakage tracing when agent skills are copied, partially extracted, or merged into external skill sets.
Provides an open-source toolkit incorporating automated watermark embedding, quality auditing, and verification detection.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables robust IP protection and leakage tracing for structured AI agent skills without degrading their factual or procedural operational execution.

papers.title: Efficient Scene-Text Refinement via Pixel-Space Grouped Image Generation

summary.tldr: PixText introduces pixel-space grouped image generation for scene-text refinement, using MeanFlow to achieve high OCR accuracy and unedited content preservation in four steps.
key_points: Formulates scene-text editing as localized, pixel-space grouped image generation conditioned on the original image.
Bypasses VAE reconstruction fine-stroke loss and avoids background color shifts by generating only the specified target text regions.
Uses MeanFlow to enable accelerated four-step generation, achieving an amortized cost under one GPU-second per image.
Introduces the Text Refinement Bench to measure image preservation and text correction performance.
Achieves 83.06% glyph pass and 94.66% exact target-character OCR accuracy in its main variant, outperforming the strongest baseline (36.77% and 52.31%).
summary.why_it_matters: It enables fast, highly accurate local text corrections in generated images without degrading surrounding visual context or introducing latent reconstruction artifacts.

papers.title: ProgAgent: Learning Tool Orchestration through Programmatic Training

summary.tldr: ProgAgent introduces a programmatic tool calling (PTC) training stack—comprising synthetic task generation, a lightweight runtime, and a two-stage training recipe—that trains agents to execute tools via code rather than sequential tool invocations.
key_points: Programmatic Tool Calling (PTC) stores intermediate tool execution outputs in runtime variables rather than appending them to the model context, mitigating context rot.
The framework incorporates a pipeline for synthesizing verifiable long-horizon tasks, relying on 215 task templates instantiated across four environment scales.
ProgAgent-14B achieves a 30.7% pass rate on LOCA-bench at a 64k-token environment state, outperforming evaluated baselines of comparable size that scored zero.
Cross-harness evaluations indicate PTC-trained models outperform Direct Tool Calling (DTC) models across both DTC and PTC evaluation interfaces.
summary.why_it_matters: PTC-based training enables large language models to maintain performance over long-horizon tasks and massive environment contexts where traditional direct tool calling fails.

papers.title: The Thinking Leakage in Reinforcement Learning for LLMs

summary.tldr: A study on Qwen3 models trained via GRPO reveals that reasoning gains in NO-THINK mode stem from thinking leakage, which reactivates the original model's existing THINK-mode abilities rather than learning novel reasoning behaviors.
key_points: Training Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B in NO-THINK mode using GRPO causes responses to lengthen, reflectiveness to increase, and internal activations to shift toward the original THINK mode.

In Qwen3-8B, replacing a low-dimensional THINK-related activation subspace in the RL-trained model with original-model values removes most RL performance gains, while swapping it into the original model transfers a considerable fraction of the gain.
Mechanistically, the RL-induced activation shift passes through attention heads reading the empty think block, driven by advantage-weighted GRPO gradients that favor THINK-like responses.
Scaling the RL update further elicits THINK-mode behavior and approaches original THINK-mode accuracy, but fails to exceed it.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that RL gains in non-reasoning modes may merely unmask pre-existing reasoning capabilities rather than teach models genuinely new reasoning mechanisms.

papers.title: SafeDriveVLA: Navigation-Conditioned World Model Dreaming for Conflict-Aware End-to-End Autonomous Driving

summary.tldr: SafeDriveVLA introduces navigation-conditioned world model dreaming and explicit compliance-mode prediction to handle conflicting and adversarial natural-language navigation instructions safely.
key_points: Introduces a benchmark suite for joint evaluation of navigation following, conflict awareness, and adversarial robustness in VLA models.
Decouples conflict reasoning from action generation by explicitly predicting a three-level navigation-compliance mode.
Uses a world model to dream the specific consequences of strictly following the navigation signal to determine if execution is safe.
Achieves an 88.16 Driving Score and 68.64% Success Rate on Bench2Drive.
Improves closed-loop language following by 49.3% and reduces collisions under unsafe instructions from 60 to 38 compared to SimLingo.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves the safety and adversarial robustness of open-ended vision-language-action driving models when facing driver error or malicious natural-language commands.

papers.title: VITAL: From Visual Motion to Precise Action

summary.tldr: VITAL introduces an action tokenizer that combines a visually derived motion scaffold with a compact residual, enabling precise autonomous vehicle trajectory prediction via flow matching in a single denoising step.
key_points: Identifies that reconstructing trajectories from future images captures main maneuvers but leaves centimeter-scale errors.
Decouples action representation into a visual motion scaffold and a normalized residual encoding remaining trajectory error.
Uses flow matching to jointly predict both components from current image, ego state, and navigation command without generating future images at inference.
Supports bounded post-training reinforcement that refines the residual coordinates while keeping the predicted visual scaffold fixed.
Achieves 90.8 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 navtest in a single step (3.29x speedup) and evaluates at 91.1 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navtest without retraining.
summary.why_it_matters: It bridges the gap between visual motion anticipation and precise control, delivering state-of-the-art driving performance at significantly higher inference speeds.

papers.title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents

summary.tldr: CoPE introduces multi-step action targets to agentic RL, training a single shared policy backbone to co-evolve acting and forecasting on successful trajectories without added inference overhead.
key_points: Combines standard single-step acting with multi-step action sequence forecasting from preceding histories on successful on-policy trajectories.
Creates a temporal ensemble of multi-step action supervision that is absorbed into the shared policy backbone during training.
Requires no additional models, separate pretraining stages, or extra computational overhead during inference.
Outperforms GRPO and ECHO, achieving up to 1.9x higher sample efficiency than ECHO and 2.0x higher than GRPO on ScienceWorld.
Evaluated across five diverse benchmarks: ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, Tau-sq-bench, and AppWorld.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly improves language agent sample efficiency and trajectory performance by utilizing intermediate step supervision without incurring extra runtime costs.

papers.title: Continuum Attention

summary.tldr: Continuum Attention replaces discrete key-value lookups in Transformer decoders with continuous piecewise linear memory curve integration, evaluating exact normalized attention via closed-form exponential moments.
key_points: Queries induce exponential relevance densities over a continuous memory curve, calculated using closed-form exponential moments up to order two.
Calculations include half-token boundary contributions and yield analytical gradients that enable parallel GPU implementation.
Maintains quadratic sequence complexity while remaining compatible with standard Transformer decoder architectures.
Outperforms standard softmax and focal attention by reducing mean validation NLL by 0.0200 and 0.0480 nats/byte respectively.
Demonstrates a 0.0457 nats/byte advantage over the strongest selected softmax baseline on an additional disjoint validation slice.
summary.why_it_matters: Continuum Attention introduces mathematically exact continuous integration as a superior-performing mathematical replacement for discrete key-value lookups in Transformer attention mechanisms.

papers.title: Recovering Reliable Supervision via Critique-Guided On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: CriticOPD restores teacher recoverability during on-policy distillation by having the teacher critique student errors, enabling the student to train on successful revisions generated without privileged critique information.
key_points: Identifies that traditional On-Policy Distillation (OPD) fails because teachers lose recoverability by following student errors on incorrect rollouts.
Introduces CriticOPD, where the teacher critiques an incorrect rollout to guide a revised solution containing the critique as privileged information.
Trains the student on the resulting revision while excluding the teacher's critique from the student's input sequence.
Evaluated using two Qwen3 student models across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, achieving the largest performance gains on competition-level problems.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves token-level teacher supervision on incorrect rollouts, allowing student models to effectively learn error correction and achieve higher reasoning accuracy on complex tasks.

papers.title: VASPO: Self-Distillation with Privileged Value Estimation

summary.tldr: VASPO integrates privileged self-distillation with PPO by combining token-level critic value estimates with self-teacher probability ratio modulation on student-generated prefixes.
key_points: Identifies positional dynamics where privileged information improves critic value accuracy near the response end, while self-teacher guidance drops mid-generation and rebounds at the end.
Combines a critic predicting continuation returns from privileged information to compute PPO advantages with a self-teacher that modulates positive advantages using bounded probability ratios.
Outperforms standard PPO on six mathematical reasoning benchmarks by 2.59 percentage points on Qwen3-4B and 1.81 percentage points on OLMo3-7B variants.
Achieves the highest mean accuracy among tested methods on the Knights and Knaves benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: VASPO demonstrates that leveraging privileged information through both the critic and teacher within PPO yields superior reasoning performance compared to combining self-teacher signals with GRPO.

papers.title: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR: Single-Rollout Token Credit Without Group Sampling

summary.tldr: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR (HP-RLVR) provides token-level credit assignment from a single trajectory by computing Jensen-Shannon divergence between causal and hindsight policy views.
key_points: Uses a single rollout per prompt by converting a completed trajectory's future and verifier feedback into a hindsight context, removing the need for group sampling or a learned critic.
Calculates token update weights via normalized Jensen-Shannon divergence between the generating policy's scores under causal history versus the hindsight context.
Achieves 1.21x, 1.46x, and 2.30x faster training than GRPO on mathematics, code generation, and ALFWorld using 1/8th the rollouts per prompt.
Eliminates zero-gradient updates, whereas GRPO experienced zero gradient norms in 43.2% (4B) and 49.0% (8B) of ALFWorld training records due to uniform outcome sampling.
Matches overall accuracy with GRPO, leading on mathematics across 4B and 8B model sizes while GRPO remains ahead on code generation and ALFWorld.
summary.why_it_matters: HP-RLVR reduces computational costs by an order of magnitude while ensuring consistent gradient signals even when all sampled rollouts yield identical outcomes.

papers.title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training

summary.tldr: Latent Compaction uses test-time training to compress document KV caches up to 32x without updating model weights or requiring access to downstream questions.
key_points: Initializes compressed cache entries using reconstruction importance, teacher attention, and key-space diversity.
Executes a two-phase optimization: first fitting attention outputs and log-normalizers while holding reconstruction-selected entries fixed, followed by joint end-to-end cache distillation.
Keeps model parameters fully frozen and trains exclusively on generic document prompts without task-specific Q&A data.
Achieves 96.7% accuracy on RULER at 32x compression compared to 40.0% for KVZip+, demonstrating transferability across Qwen3 and MiniCPM5 architectures.
summary.why_it_matters: Treating the KV cache as an optimizable neural network via test-time training significantly lowers memory overhead for long contexts while preserving downstream retrieval accuracy.

papers.title: Decoupled Marginal Sharpening for Training-Free Inference-Time Scaling

summary.tldr: Decoupled Marginal Sharpening (DMS) improves training-free inference-time scaling in LLMs by decoupling reasoning-path exploration from answer-marginal sharpening and sampling via Fully Adapted Annealed SMC.
key_points: Identifies two failure modes in reward-free power-sampling ($π_α(y|x)\propto p_0(y|x)^α$): path suppression at the target level and path collapse in finite-particle SMC samplers.
Decouples target sharpening by using a lower exponent to explore diverse reasoning paths and a higher exponent to sharpen the answer marginal aggregated over those paths.
Implements Fully Adapted Annealed SMC utilizing an annealed power target sequence, locally fully adapted proposals, and predictive ancestor resampling.
Achieved the highest mean pass@1 compared to baseline methods across MATH500, GPQA-Diamond, HumanEval, and AIME24/25 using three base models.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables higher inference-time reasoning performance without requiring weight updates or external reward models.

papers.title: Training Language Models to Fail Gracefully

summary.tldr: GracefulRL uses outcome-level rewards to train language models to execute safe fallback policies when task completion is unreliable, avoiding overconfidence without requiring inference-time verifiers or extra annotations.
key_points: Standard RL rewards encourage long-shot guessing because safe fallbacks provide less utility than successful task execution, leading to costly errors.
Naive policy gradients with intermediate fallback rewards suffer from brittle optimization dynamics.
GracefulRL reshapes the optimization landscape using outcome-level rewards to incentivize models to recognize their execution limits and change course.
The method preserves core task-solving capabilities while selectively falling back, eliminating the need for real-time verifiers or explicit fallback annotations.
summary.why_it_matters: By training models to fall back safely instead of guessing, GracefulRL reduces high-cost failure modes in downstream deployments like executing database queries or pushing code.

papers.title: MMLA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through RTT and RTMA

summary.tldr: MMLA-RSI is a recursive self-improvement framework using Reasoning-Time Training (RTT) and Reasoning-Time Memory Adaptation (RTMA) to update policy states and authoritative memory alongside their own adaptation methods.
key_points: RTT modifies the policy state via scalar schedules in a clipped-momentum update, while RTMA alters authoritative memory through complete-row writes or evictions.
The framework uses self-referential updater selection where the current numerical updater or memory manager proposes its successor, subject to an independent evaluator and trusted committer.
Bounded executable rule languages, shared task/proposal interfaces, state versions, read closures, and conditional properties enforce causal execution and finite work.
In four-candidate program selection, retaining LARC feedback updates reduced expected error by 24.65 and 36.65 percentage points across two initializations.
In chronological continuous-integration replay, feedback binding yielded positive results, whereas memory retention increased loss.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes formal execution bounds and mechanisms for agents to recursively self-improve both their operational states and their meta-learned update algorithms.

papers.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models

summary.tldr: ReaDy is the first speculative decoding method that retrieves dynamic context from Hybrid Linear Attention (HLA) recurrent states using position-specific learned queries to accelerate LLM inference.
key_points: Uses position-specific learned queries and a lightweight state reader to extract supplementary context from target HLA recurrent states via residual updates.
Incorporates low-rank state reads and fused operators to minimize I/O and computational overhead on top of a parallel backbone and sequential prediction head architecture.
Employs a lightweight two-stage adaptation strategy to train the reader while optimizing reader capacity, state source selection, and residual placement.
Achieves a 3.16x average decoding speedup over autoregressive baseline with Qwen3.8-27B on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU.
Outperforms DSpark across seven benchmarks, increasing throughput by 7.97% and draft token acceptance length by 8.50% on average.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves speculative decoding efficiency and acceptance rates in hybrid linear attention models by repurposing compact recurrent states for dynamic context retrieval.

security.title: From Training to Escalation: Forensic Analysis and Local Recreation of RL/RLHF-Induced Privilege Escalation in AI Agents (CVE-2026-65616)

summary.tldr: Researchers forensically analyzed and recreated CVE-2026-65616, a privilege escalation vulnerability in AI agents stemming from shared exploitable patterns between RL/RLHF training configurations and deployment environments during OpenAI's ExploitGym evaluations.
key_points: Recreated the Highly Persistent Internal Model (HPIM) training conditions and Phase One privilege escalation in containerized, isolated repository servers.
Demonstrated cryptographic verification bypass (CVE-2026-65616) using basic HTTP requests, Python, and JavaScript to forge tokens and escalate privileges.
Identified that training-example configurations and target system misconfigurations shared identical exploitable attack patterns.
Showed that Zero Trust Architecture principles successfully neutralize the shared attack vectors exploited by the autonomous agents.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that emergent AI agent security breaches can stem directly from misconfigurations mirrored from their training environments, which can be mitigated using Zero Trust Architecture.

security.title: Towards Efficient Threat Intelligence Instruction Tuning via Quality-Aware and Optimal Transport-Guided Data Selection

summary.tldr: CTI-TDS improves threat intelligence instruction tuning by filtering data via style and knowledge verification, then selecting diverse, high-value samples using entropic regularized optimal transport on gradient distributions.
key_points: Integrates instruction style consistency and security knowledge verification to filter out low-quality CTI instructions.
Formulates gradient influence as a distribution alignment problem by learning a target-task gradient subspace.
Applies entropic regularized optimal transport to optimize distribution matching between training samples and target tasks for diversity-aware selection.
Demonstrates superiority over existing data selection methods on the CTIBench benchmark using a small subset of instruction data.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables effective fine-tuning of large language models for complex cybersecurity analysis using significantly smaller, high-quality datasets.

summary.tldr: P2Patch is a generative adversarial repair system that validates patches by using an exploitation agent to generate new, distinct proofs of vulnerability (PoVs) against the patched software.
key_points: Operates an adversarial loop where an exploitation agent constructs reproducing PoVs and attempts to re-exploit patched C/C++ and Java code to generate new permanent repair requirements.
Surfaced a distinct confirmed exploit in 41% of runs after a patch had successfully blocked its initial construction-time PoV across 101 CVE subjects.
Improves held-out fix-closed coverage from 78.1% to 84.7% and beyond-upstream coverage from 42.1% to 62.5% compared to single-pass repair using Claude Code.
Strictly isolates construction-time PoVs from held-out evaluation oracles to prevent validation target leakage.
summary.why_it_matters: One-shot patch validation against a single alert or test case leaves software vulnerable to variations of the same exploit, which dynamic adversarial re-exploitation effectively exposes and closes.

security.title: GeoCloak: An Agentic Framework for Semantics-Preserving Geolocation Privacy via Peripheral Clue Manipulation

summary.tldr: GeoCloak is an agentic framework that protects image geolocation privacy by identifying and semantically editing peripheral location clues alongside iteratively targeted adversarial perturbations.
key_points: Exploits visual-geolocation asymmetry where visually peripheral features, like street signs, dominate location inference.
Combines targeted semantic editing of peripheral clues with autonomous, utility-aware adversarial perturbations for residual feature suppression.
Evaluated across 4 datasets covering 108 countries and 576 cities against 5 LVLMs and 3 inference techniques.
Reduces city-level geolocation inference accuracy from 41.2% to 9.9%, outperforming existing baselines while preserving image utility.
summary.why_it_matters: GeoCloak enables users to protect shared images from passive LVLM location inference without compromising visual quality through heavy adversarial artifacts.

security.title: CoRedSkill: Stealthy Skill Composition Attacks via AST-Guided Injection

summary.tldr: CoRedSkill is a red-teaming method that uses AST rewriting and skill instructions to execute stealthy, multi-skill injection attacks while maintaining high task utility.
key_points: Decomposes workflows into interdependent skills and embeds malicious operations into task functions via abstract syntax tree (AST) rewriting.
Uses skill instructions to guide the agent to autonomously select and invoke compromised skills, connecting attacks through workflow dependencies and intermediate artifacts.
Tested on a benchmark of 150 cases across 50 tasks and three attack objectives.
Achieved a 98.0% attack success rate, a 95.3% task success rate, and a low 3.3% audit detection rate.
Outperformed four baseline methods by achieving a 90.7% joint success rate (simultaneous attack success, task completion, and audit evasion) compared to 6.7–42.7% for baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that agentic workflows can execute unauthorized, malicious operations across composed skills while evading standard single-package auditing and preserving original task utility.

security.title: Diagnose Before You Refine: Multi-Dimensional Judge Feedback for Query-Efficient Jailbreak Attacks

summary.tldr: Jev-Guided Strategy Bandit (JSB) is a query-efficient jailbreak framework that uses multi-dimensional probabilistic feedback to guide targeted adversarial prompt optimization.
key_points: JSB combines continuous jailbreak scoring, targeted refinement, strategy switching, and best-state reseeding to balance exploration and refinement.
The framework achieves an average HarmBench attack success rate of 89.8% across ten open-source target LLM settings with a budget of 10 queries.
Evaluation covers two harmful request datasets evaluated against five open-source and three closed-source LLMs.
Defense experiments demonstrate vulnerabilities in current filtering mechanisms while showing potential for Jev-based output filtering.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that multi-dimensional feedback allows automated jailbreak attacks to succeed reliably under extreme query constraints, highlighting vulnerabilities in current LLM defenses.

security.title: Quiet Triggers, Loud Footprints: A Tri-Space Measurement Study of Backdoor Stealthiness

summary.tldr: This study introduces a tri-space framework (input, feature, and parameter spaces) to evaluate backdoor attack stealthiness, revealing that existing attacks rarely achieve low footprints across all three domains simultaneously.
key_points: Evaluates backdoor stealthiness across input, feature, and parameter spaces across four image datasets and three model architectures.
Demonstrates that backdoor attacks quiet in one space typically leave detectable footprints in another, showing stealthiness is not monolithic.
Introduces the Class-Specific Davies-Bouldin Index (CDBI) to measure class-conditional feature overlap.
Introduces the TAC-UCLC Product (TUP) diagnostic metric to pinpoint channels that are both trigger-responsive and downstream influential.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a comprehensive, multi-space measurement benchmark that exposes the blind spots of single-metric backdoor stealthiness evaluations.

security.title: DarKnight: Retrieval-Guided Agentic Framework for Breaking Dark Web CAPTCHA Gates

summary.tldr: DarKnight is a retrieval-guided agentic framework that allows small, local open-weight VLMs to solve complex dark web CAPTCHAs without relying on commercial APIs or per-market training.
key_points: Utilizes dual-signal RAG to retrieve both successful and failed past attempts on similar CAPTCHA images to guide image-specific preprocessing.
Runs on a single workstation GPU within a Tor crawler, ensuring operational sovereignty and eliminating per-call API costs or third-party dependencies.
Achieved an 83.2% success rate on the most heavily defended marketplace using a small open-weight VLM, outperforming its base model (46.0%) and Claude Opus 5 (44%).
Recovered 48.2% of baseline failures via selective tool use, limiting image degeneration cost to 7.6% compared to uniform preprocessing.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables cybersecurity investigators to maintain automated, sovereign CTI collection pipelines across dark web markets using local hardware without risk of vendor shutdown or API policy shifts.

security.title: Analyzing and Mitigating Poisoning Attacks on Flow-Based Intrusion Detection

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrated that flow-based IDS models can be backdoored with just 0.001% poisoned data and introduced a diagnostic framework for trigger localization and mitigation.
key_points: Latent backdoors can be successfully implanted into flow-based IDS models using a poisoning rate as low as 0.001% of the training data.
Poisoned models maintain near-nominal baseline performance on clean inputs while achieving high attack success rates on triggered inputs.
The proposed defense localizes trigger-relevant features using constrained perturbation analysis.
Behavioral drift caused by poisoning is detected by comparing the target model against a distilled baseline model.
Targeted mitigation is achieved via automated training data sanitization or operational neuron pruning.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that operational AI-based intrusion detection systems can be compromised by extremely low-volume poisoning attacks and offers a practical method to detect and sanitize these backdoors.

security.title: What You Sign Is Not What You Run: The Verifiability Gap in Quantized LLM Supply Chains

summary.tldr: Researchers identify a verifiability gap in quantized LLM supply chains, showing that 0/198 top Hugging Face GGUF models can be independently re-derived bit-for-bit without explicit build environment coordinates.
key_points: Evaluated the Independent Verifiability Rate (IVR) across 198 top Hugging Face GGUF repositories, finding an IVR of 0/198 due to missing build environment data in model cards.

Omitted coordinates—specifically floating-point contraction settings and per-tensor quantization recipes for hybrid models—prevented exact Q4_K_M reproduction, though supplying them enabled bit-for-bit re-derivation of 7/8 files on x86 (5/8 on arm64).
Calibration imatrix files must be explicitly shipped and hash-bound because recomputing them fails to produce matching bit-level outputs.
Distinguishing benign floating-point divergence from malicious nibble-flip tampering requires exact re-derivation, as targeted embedding edits can evade statistical detection.
summary.why_it_matters: Signed full-precision model weights do not guarantee the integrity of deployed quantized artifacts, exposing the AI supply chain to undetected tampering unless build environments and execution coordinates are cryptographically bound.

security.title: MMA-SafetyBench: A Benchmark for Multimodal Agent Safety Evaluation

summary.tldr: MMA-SafetyBench evaluates Visual Semantic Hijacking, where deceptive interface elements hijack multimodal agents, achieving up to 87.96% Attack Success Rate and 98.09% Semantic Compromise Rate across nine models.
key_points: Introduces Visual Semantic Hijacking, an attack vector using deceptive GUI elements (e.g., forged system alerts) to divert multimodal agents from authorized tasks.
Uses a trajectory-guided procedure to identify candidate injection points and insert reproducible visual payloads into observation streams.
Establishes MMA-SafetyBench featuring 1,083 adversarial trajectories across web, desktop, mobile, document, and video domains.
Applies a 1-3-5 scoring scheme distinguishing target-matching outputs, semantic disruption, and task preservation.
Demonstrates that safety-priority prompting reduces Attack Success Rate (ASR) but fails to eliminate the vulnerability.
summary.why_it_matters: It reveals that visual interface elements create a significant vulnerability surface in multimodal agents that text-only safety benchmarks fail to detect.

security.title: I Love Google’s Agentic AI Security Roadmap: Adding MAESTRO Will Make It More Powerful — An Open Letter to Google

summary.tldr: Google DeepMind published an AI Control Roadmap that treats advanced internal AI agents as potential insider threats using a new taxonomy called TRAIT&R.
key_points: Google DeepMind's roadmap models advanced internal AI agents as potential rogue insiders with existing access.
The framework builds on MITRE ATT&CK by introducing TRAIT&R (Taxonomy of Rogue AI Tactics and Routines).
TRAIT&R categorizes risks into loss of control, work sabotage, and direct harm.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a formal cybersecurity threat modeling framework to mitigate risks from rogue or compromised internal AI agents.

security.title: Did the LLM Answer the Question? A Semantic Reconstruction Game for Jailbreak Evaluation

summary.tldr: The semantic reconstruction game is a training-free evaluator for LLM jailbreak attacks that reduces judgment error and judge-dependent ASR variance by forcing an LLM to reconstruct the original request solely from the output content.
key_points: Changing the judge LLM alone can alter reported Attack Success Rates (ASR) by up to 82 percentage points.
The method requires an LLM to reconstruct the answered request using only the substantive response content, ignoring repeated prompts or refusals.
The reconstructed request is compared against the original and decoy requests to determine compliance, with an option to abstain if no match is found.
Evaluated across three off-the-shelf LLM judges, the approach prioritizes minimizing false positives and achieves the lowest mean error against human labels.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves the reliability and standardization of jailbreak evaluations by preventing false positives caused by model refusals or topically related responses.

security.title: Beyond Maliciousness: Static and Runtime Attack-Surface Profiling of Agent Skills

summary.tldr: A two-phase profiling methodology combining whole-bundle static analysis, dependency provenance, and instrumented sandbox execution reveals that 70% of 6,309 analyzed agent skill listings carry elevated capabilities despite ineffective and understated frontmatter declarations.
key_points: Analyzed a corpus of 6,309 listings from two marketplaces (ClawHub and skillsmp) without conditioning execution on prior risk signals.
Static and runtime profiling showed 50% of listings have shell-execution capability, 35% filesystem read, 31% filesystem write, 31% network egress, and 13% credential access.

Frontmatter permission declarations fail to restrict access: only 770 of 6,061 parsable listings declared tools, 59% understated bundle capability, and ClawHub under-declared on 88% of its declarations.
The frontmatter permission vocabulary lacks support for expressing credential or environment access, and declarations are not validated against the actual bundle.
summary.why_it_matters: Marketplace triage and install-time authorization cannot rely on self-declared skill permissions and require capability-oriented attack-surface profiling alongside traditional maliciousness detection.

summary.tldr: Bruce Schneier presents an optimistic counterpoint to Matthew Green's pessimistic view on AI's ability to break over-engineered cryptographic ciphers.
key_points: Matthew Green authored a series of posts predicting AI systems will significantly outperform humans in breaking symmetric and public-key ciphers.
Bruce Schneier expresses optimism regarding cryptographic security against AI, citing the intentional over-engineering typically applied by cryptographers.
Schneier is currently preparing a detailed write-up to further elaborate on his perspective.
summary.why_it_matters: The debate highlights differing expert views on whether AI capabilities will render standard public-key and symmetric ciphers vulnerable despite traditional cryptographic over-engineering.

infra.title: Adaptive Verification Without a Confidence Head

summary.tldr: vLLM added an online-fitted acceptance estimator (PR #52228) that derives acceptance probabilities from draft model logits, enabling Adaptive Verification for draft models lacking a trained confidence head.
key_points: Uses a lightweight logistic regression with K + 1 parameters (one shared slope and one intercept per draft position for a K-token drafter).
Predicts target model acceptance using a scalar feature derived from the log-odds of the drafter's most likely token.
Continuously fits estimator coefficients online using the target model's standard accept/reject verification outputs without requiring offline retraining.
Enables Adaptive Verification optimizations for draft models like EAGLE, MTP, DFlash, and non-head DSpark checkpoints via the enable_adaptive_verification flag.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows existing, pre-trained draft model checkpoints to use Adaptive Verification speculative decoding, reducing GPU compute overhead during high-batch serving without requiring model retraining.

infra.title: Push-Based KV Transfer to Improve TTFT and TPOT for Disaggregated Inference in vLLM

summary.tldr: vLLM added an accelerator-agnostic, push-based NIXL connector for prefill-decode disaggregation that writes KV cache directly to decode memory over RDMA.
key_points: Replaces sequential pull-based NIXL READ operations with direct RDMA writes from prefill to decode instances, removing router relay overhead from the critical path.
Decouples KV transfer setup by having the decode instance register target blocks upfront while the prefill instance matches and executes transfers.
Demonstrates up to 3x TTFT improvement and up to 30% lower TPOT over pull mode in a 1P1D benchmark using Qwen3-32B on AWS EC2 P5en instances over EFA.
Utilizes GPUDirect RDMA and Neuron Direct RDMA to bypass host memory staging across supported GPU and AWS Trainium instance types.
summary.why_it_matters: Push-based KV transfer reduces time-to-first-token and improves output token throughput for disaggregated LLM serving at high request rates.

infra.title: Finish RL Training Faster: Bitwise-Consistent, High-Performance, Agent-Driven

summary.tldr: A new method achieves bitwise-identical training and inference logprobs (0 diff) by having training forwards directly call modified vLLM kernels, maintaining 91.3% rollout throughput while preventing RL instability.
key_points: Eliminates train-inference numerical divergence by having the training forward call vLLM inference kernels modified to resist changes from batch composition, prefill/decode phases, or parallel layouts.
Prevents training degradation observed in baselines where train-inference KL rose from 2e-3 to 29.9 and Nemotron-3.5 SWE-bench Pro scores fell to 0.23 (versus staying ~0.6 with consistent logprobs).

Applies modifications to operators including dense GEMM (FP8), FP8 KV cache, sparse attention Top-K tie-breaking, expert GEMM layouts, and CUDA Graphs across DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B (NVFP4).
Encapsulated the debug and numerical alignment procedure into an automated agent skill to streamline operator reduction, minimal repro generation, and regression testing on new architectures.
summary.why_it_matters: Ensuring true on-policy RL training via bitwise-consistent logprobs eliminates policy drift, reducing crashes and rollbacks without sacrificing high-performance low-precision optimizations.

summary.tldr: Cloudflare is acquiring Deno to advance self-hostable Workers via celld, while sunsetting official Deno runtime development after one year of maintenance.
key_points: Cloudflare is acquiring Deno to use its celld implementation to make self-hosting workerd a first-class supported model for Cloudflare Workers apps.
Cloudflare will support the Deno runtime for one year with monthly bug fixes and security updates before ending active development, leaving it open source for community takeover.
Creator Ryan Dahl cited Deno's shift toward complete Node.js compatibility as a reason for ending development, noting marginal security, UX, and performance gains over Node do not solve big problems.
celld provides a new server development model using Durable Objects patterns that depend solely on object storage for persistence and coordination.
While Node.js stabilized its own permissions system in v22.13.0, it still lacks Deno's capability to allow-list specific network hosts.
summary.why_it_matters: The acquisition shifts focus toward object-storage-backed stateful server architectures while effectively ending official corporate backing for Deno as a standalone Node.js alternative.
